description: This line plot, titled “Ablation Study on HateXplain Dataset,” illustrates the performance of five different model variants across three evaluation metrics: a generic “Metric (%)” (represented by a purple line with circular markers), “Recall” (blue line with circular markers), and “F1-score” (brown line with circular markers), as shown in the legend. The x-axis, labeled “Model Variants,” lists five categorical conditions: “Full model (Ours),” “w/o Prompt,” “w/o Augmentation,” “w/o Attention,” and “w/o Prompt & Augmentation.” The y-axis, labeled “Metric (%),” is a linear scale ranging from 56 to 66, with major gridlines at 58, 60, 62, 64, and 66. For the “Full model (Ours),” the purple line starts at 65.45%, the blue line at 65.56%, and the brown line at 65.49%. Removing the prompt causes all three metrics to drop sharply: the purple line falls to 61.06%, the blue line to 59.64%, and the brown line to 60.16%. When augmentation is removed, the purple line rises to 62.22%, the blue line to 63.75%, and the brown line to 62.63%. Removing attention causes the purple line to increase to 64.06%, while the blue line drops to 59.17% and the brown line to 59.67%. Finally, removing both prompt and augmentation results in the purple line reaching 65.44%, the blue line falling to 56.82%, and the brown line to 57.74%. The plot visually demonstrates how each component affects the different metrics, with some components having opposing effects on different metrics.
